text.p: Diversified manufacturer Pacific Dunlop Ltd said on Friday that it had completed its current rationalisation programme.
"We've brought in and rationalised the company as far as we really care to rationalise it at this time," Pacific Dunlop's chairman John Gough told reporters
The restructuring of Pacific Dunlop over the last 18 months has seen the company divest itself of about A$1.5 billion worth of assets.
Its divestments included Pasta House, its 51 percent stake in the Australian and New Zealand subsidiary of German sportswear maker Adidas AG and the float of its bionic ear unit Cochlear Ltd.
"In all of the divisions, that we've sold in recent times, we have virtually, with one or two tiny exceptions, got back every dollar of assets for those," Gough said.
He added that the only significant loss made in its current divestment program would be on the sale of U.S. unit Telectronics Pacing Systems, which is currently under negotiation.
